chapters.title: Invocations & Spring Songs (Zingkum Hao Kaphok)
chapters.summary: Hokharai war-cry and spring arrival songs heralded by Sampheirok and Koktui.
chapters.tangkhul_text: AE-HE! Phamei yameisa HE... HE. O--O-HU-O! Ilongnao laa sa usa, Kashishoklu, kaphazanglu--O--Hui-O-hui! O, kazingkum ura, o, kazingkum ura, o, hungnaovayo luithuimihaolu; Mamanaomara, hungnaovayo luithuimashunga; Sampheirokna riri rakhonga, koktui vana zingkum phungraya!
chapters.english_translation: Hokharai invocation: May the better be ours! Let us sing, may evil depart and divine goodness enter! O, spring has begun! Your highness, sow the seeds for the year; royal venture is just and timely; The Sampheirok sings melodiously and the cuckoo heralds the arrival of the fruitful year!
grammar_points: Reduplication in bird call onomatopoeia ('riri rakhonga').
comprehension_questions: What is Hokharai and when is it performed?
Which birds announce the arrival of spring?

chapters.title: Tarung Carrying & Monument Construction Songs
chapters.summary: Dragging the monumental Tarung tree from the forest and erecting megaliths.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, yarso thingrei vakhang, thingpitang tak ungrall yaronnao, thingreiva ungreilu! Seichang kharaei hangmi phalungra, phanora vashatta chaklen meikan naona kacheka, lumlao sakda vakhuiphalungra. O, Kashongta phung-o, maranla saya; ilangkaso machilo, I wui luiyi kaya lhuiito, I wui chumrei hjorphiya!
chapters.english_translation: O young men, lift the mighty tree! The twigs bend, pull together with sturdy cane ropes; The sacrificial mithun is provided, the augury bird Chaklen gave favorable omens; carry home the Tarung! I built this house from humble beginnings; my terrace fields are fertile and granary full!
grammar_points: Collective working rhythm in dragging chants.
comprehension_questions: What bird's call determines the auspiciousness of monument hauling?
What animal is sacrificed for the Tarung?

chapters.title: Ceremonial Dance & Hornbill Movements (Pheishon Laa)
chapters.summary: Dance steps modeled on the flight and wingbeats of the great Indian hornbill.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, iram hongreili, Mafathing kasui kharipna; Ngachamching arang shangkaya, arangchi khili kachanlo? Mafathei channa, arangkho arangkhon ngashing leishiya; Thuingashing, kashung shanghaowa.
chapters.english_translation: In our ancient forests, the majestic Mafathing trees spread their wide canopy; Upon their boughs perch the great hornbills; why have they gathered in numbers? For the ripe Mafa fruits they have flown; with rhythmic wingbeats they soar towards the mountain peaks!
grammar_points: Choreographic terminology encoded in song lyrics.
comprehension_questions: What bird inspires the choreography of Pheishon?
Why is the hornbill culturally sacred to Tangkhuls?

chapters.title: Maiden Dances & Youth Festivals (Yarra Laa)
chapters.summary: Laa Khanganui maiden dances and the Yarra spring festival of the youth.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kazingkum huimailo aria, shivanaoli khina sale? Kha shingnai rao vasaya, he ring khaya zak matheiya. Kongrali theo theo, ilongnaova khithing kaphato? Ilongnaova longthing kaphana, meishum kapamnao zangyo!
chapters.english_translation: Let the seasons turn in gentleness! Maidens dance in the village square in graceful innocence. What merry voices echo by the stream? The youth gather firewood for the annual Yarra celebration!
comprehension_questions: In which months is the Yarra festival celebrated?
What activity do the youth undertake during Yarra?

chapters.title: Agriculture, Terrace Labor & Cowherd Songs
chapters.summary: Luisom paddy planting chants and Sei Hom cowherd ballads of solitary orphans.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, I siluisa, I siluisa khinashai? I makreira khina mang, makreira sangralu; Shama maran saluira. Ava khaho malei, aya kaho malei, seihom langphaizaya; Shok reo rangpamshona, silui shur khani chi kachui laga yaronnao chara horlama.
chapters.english_translation: Who will feast on my buffalo meat, who will drink my aged rice beer? Pour generously for the laborers! No parents call my name; upon the high grassy slopes I herd buffalos alone from dawn till dusk, Tending the herds while silent tears trace lines upon my face.
grammar_points: Rhetorical questions in festive work songs.
Poignant elegiac tone in pastoral chants.
comprehension_questions: What contrast is drawn between festive terrace planting and cowherd life?

chapters.title: Martial Ballads & Head-hunting Epics (Ral Laa)
chapters.summary: Ancient heroic victory chants and warrior prowess of Lunghar and Ringui.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, atung shangla rai sakashiyavo, Lunghar yaron ni chiya! Azing takha rai sakashiyavo, Ringui yaron ni chiya! Shangching Shangshak na ili khachitna chiya, shimin kayang ra mahon shok! Kharing sing singa, ili mangakatshelu!
chapters.english_translation: Behold in the northern heights the gallant warriors of Lunghar stand ready! In the southern ranges the brave youths of Ringui guard the mountain passes; They fear me as the tiger of the forest; challenge me not, for our victory shout resounds!
comprehension_questions: Which two villages are celebrated as warrior centres?

chapters.title: Traditional Love Romances (Shimreishang & Maitonphi)
chapters.summary: The immortal romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi in antiphonal dialogue.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Avayo avayo, makhamalu, Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa. Laishikhavai chi lunamlizang ngaroksa; Coi marongthei reola khuisingda lung ringa. Ameishang Ameishang, Ira kachangli thuiulu; Maitonphi, pangthui haosa, ini lungchan malaihaosa.
chapters.english_translation: Elders, do not forbid! For sweet Maitonphi alone does my heart beat in devotion; Though adverse circumstances part us in this earthly life, our love remains green like the mountain pine. Beloved Ameishang, farewell on this mortal shore; in the spirit realm beyond, we shall part no more.
comprehension_questions: What plant symbolizes unyielding love in the ballad?
How does the story conclude in traditional belief?

chapters.title: Weaving Songs, Festive Banquets & Bedtime Chants
chapters.summary: Back-strap loom weaving (Themsak), traditional shawls, and evening chants (Pet Laa).
chapters.tangkhul_text: O Tangkhul ngalanao yanglu yanglu, sak kasa kathemma themma; Haora chi yaron kachonna, Phangyai rah Tangkhul kashanna! Phungcham vana ratha apamva rarona, phanishida tarikhana vaotun; Nali ungthuilo, sami ngachiya, i ram kashamshiraro.
chapters.english_translation: Behold the skilled Tangkhul maidens weaving traditional textiles with masterly artistry! The black-and-red Haora shawl is for valiant young men, and the Phangyai skirt for graceful women. Evening settles over the ridges of Phungcham; put aside your tools and find peaceful sleep.
comprehension_questions: What is Haora and who wears it?
What is Phangyai and what colors define it?

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Invocations & Spring Songs (Zingkum Hao Kaphok)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: AE-HE! Phamei yameisa HE... HE. O--O-HU-O! Ilongnao laa sa usa, Kashishoklu, kaphazanglu--O--Hui-O-hui! O, kazingkum ura, o, kazingkum ura, o, hungnaovayo luithuimihaolu; Mamanaomara, hungnaovayo luithuimashunga; Sampheirokna riri rakhonga, koktui vana zingkum phungraya!
excerpts.translation_en: Hokharai invocation: May the better be ours! Let us sing, may evil depart and divine goodness enter! O, spring has begun! Your highness, sow the seeds for the year; royal venture is just and timely; The Sampheirok sings melodiously and the cuckoo heralds the arrival of the fruitful year!

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Tarung Carrying & Monument Construction Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: O, yarso thingrei vakhang, thingpitang tak ungrall yaronnao, thingreiva ungreilu! Seichang kharaei hangmi phalungra, phanora vashatta chaklen meikan naona kacheka, lumlao sakda vakhuiphalungra. O, Kashongta phung-o, maranla saya; ilangkaso machilo, I wui luiyi kaya lhuiito, I wui chumrei hjorphiya!
excerpts.translation_en: O young men, lift the mighty tree! The twigs bend, pull together with sturdy cane ropes; The sacrificial mithun is provided, the augury bird Chaklen gave favorable omens; carry home the Tarung! I built this house from humble beginnings; my terrace fields are fertile and granary full!

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Ceremonial Dance & Hornbill Movements (Pheishon Laa)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: O, iram hongreili, Mafathing kasui kharipna; Ngachamching arang shangkaya, arangchi khili kachanlo? Mafathei channa, arangkho arangkhon ngashing leishiya; Thuingashing, kashung shanghaowa.
excerpts.translation_en: In our ancient forests, the majestic Mafathing trees spread their wide canopy; Upon their boughs perch the great hornbills; why have they gathered in numbers? For the ripe Mafa fruits they have flown; with rhythmic wingbeats they soar towards the mountain peaks!

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Maiden Dances & Youth Festivals (Yarra Laa)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kazingkum huimailo aria, shivanaoli khina sale? Kha shingnai rao vasaya, he ring khaya zak matheiya. Kongrali theo theo, ilongnaova khithing kaphato? Ilongnaova longthing kaphana, meishum kapamnao zangyo!
excerpts.translation_en: Let the seasons turn in gentleness! Maidens dance in the village square in graceful innocence. What merry voices echo by the stream? The youth gather firewood for the annual Yarra celebration!

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Agriculture, Terrace Labor & Cowherd Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: O, I siluisa, I siluisa khinashai? I makreira khina mang, makreira sangralu; Shama maran saluira. Ava khaho malei, aya kaho malei, seihom langphaizaya; Shok reo rangpamshona, silui shur khani chi kachui laga yaronnao chara horlama.
excerpts.translation_en: Who will feast on my buffalo meat, who will drink my aged rice beer? Pour generously for the laborers! No parents call my name; upon the high grassy slopes I herd buffalos alone from dawn till dusk, Tending the herds while silent tears trace lines upon my face.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Martial Ballads & Head-hunting Epics (Ral Laa)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: O, atung shangla rai sakashiyavo, Lunghar yaron ni chiya! Azing takha rai sakashiyavo, Ringui yaron ni chiya! Shangching Shangshak na ili khachitna chiya, shimin kayang ra mahon shok! Kharing sing singa, ili mangakatshelu!
excerpts.translation_en: Behold in the northern heights the gallant warriors of Lunghar stand ready! In the southern ranges the brave youths of Ringui guard the mountain passes; They fear me as the tiger of the forest; challenge me not, for our victory shout resounds!

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Avayo avayo, makhamalu, Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa. Laishikhavai chi lunamlizang ngaroksa; Coi marongthei reola khuisingda lung ringa. Ameishang Ameishang, Ira kachangli thuiulu; Maitonphi, pangthui haosa, ini lungchan malaihaosa.
excerpts.translation_en: Elders, do not forbid! For sweet Maitonphi alone does my heart beat in devotion; Though adverse circumstances part us in this earthly life, our love remains green like the mountain pine. Beloved Ameishang, farewell on this mortal shore; in the spirit realm beyond, we shall part no more.
